causebase_summary: Guildhouse (legal name: Craftsouth: Centre For Contemporary Craft & Design Inc) is a South Australian arts organisation supporting visual artists, craft makers and designers. It operates across South Australia and beyond and is supported by the South Australian Government through CreateSA and by the Visual Arts, Craft and Design Partnership Framework. Guildhouse delivers fellowships, peer-to-peer mentorships, direct artist commissions, professional development workshops, studio residencies and tailored professional services; it presents work to public audiences, issues calls for participation and publishes artist toolkits. The organisation also undertakes sector development activities including advocacy and targeted research, and maintains a membership of more than 1,200 practising artists.

data.SummaryOfActivities: 2025 was a year defined by artistic excellence, collective achievement and renewed purpose for Guildhouse. Guided by our new Strategic Plan and Manifesto, we stepped forward with conviction as sector leaders supporting the career development and livelihoods of South Australian artists at  every stage of their career.  Our suite of nationally recognised artistic programs continued to advance practice, encourage experimentation and increase visibility for visual artists, craft makers and designers. Whilst our unique exhibition series, in traditional and non-traditional gallery spaces, connected South Australian artists and their work to new  audiences of over 2 million people.  In 2025 Guildhouse provided an ambitious suite of tailored support services and meaningful employment for artists, generating more than $1.2 million in direct income for artists, artisans and creative  workers.
